About this site

This website shows the Kids Coding course on the web. It is built from the same source files as the printed workbooks, so the pages and the PDFs always match.

Privacy

There are no accounts, no analytics, no cookies and no adverts. Nothing you type is sent anywhere. Your progress ticks and display choices (dark mode, easy-read font) are saved only in your own browser, on your own device.

Accessibility

We aim for WCAG 2.2 level AA. In practice that means:

  • All pictures have a text description, and the Scratch scripts are described block by block.
  • You can use the whole site with a keyboard. Press Tab to move and Enter to open things. The first link on every page skips the menu.
  • Colors come from a color-blind-safe palette, and nothing relies on color alone.
  • Use the Easy-read font button at the top for the dyslexia-friendly Lexend font with wider spacing, and the Dark mode button if bright pages are hard to read.
  • Lesson pages print neatly: use your browser's print command, or download the PDF.

If something is hard to use, please tell the person who runs your course so it can be fixed.

How the site is built

A script reads the course's LaTeX and Python source files and turns the student parts into web pages. Teacher-only material and the solutions are never read or published. The build checks the finished site and stops if any private material would be included.

Credits and licenses

  • Fonts: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Mono (Braille Institute) and Lexend Deca (Lexend Project), all under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, served from this site.
  • Pictures and diagrams: all original, drawn for this course in TikZ and the Scratch block package, and converted to SVG. Slide images come from the parent deck, also original.
  • Icons and logo: original simple shapes drawn for this site.
  • Colors: the Okabe-Ito color-blind-safe palette.
  • Scratch is a project of the Scratch Foundation and Python is a trademark of the Python Software Foundation. This course is not affiliated with either.

Change log

Current version 1.1.0, updated 2026-11-08.

All notable changes to the Kids Coding website and course materials. The website version is in VERSION. Dates are in ISO format.

1.1.0 - 2026-11-08

Levels 2 and 3, projects and resources.

  • Level 2 and Level 3: 12 week pages each, 68 more exercise pages with three hints each, descriptions for all 45 remaining diagrams.
  • Final project pages for all three levels: brief, plan sheet, rubric and the starter files to download. Teacher-only material and solutions are not published.
  • Resources: Mac setup guide (Scratch, Thonny, Python, pytest, git), troubleshooting, cheat sheets and a combined glossary for the three levels, printable progress trackers, and notes for families for each level.
  • Quality gates now cover all three levels.

1.0.0 - 2026-11-08

First public version of the website, generated from the course sources.

  • Home, For parents, Curriculum and Level 1 pages (12 week pages, 38 exercise pages with hints).
  • Parent research page, slide gallery and FAQ generated from the parent deck and its bibliography.
  • Each level now runs 10 to 12 weeks; the two buffer sessions are optional.
  • Student-facing PDFs for download; teacher-only material and solutions are never published.

Kids Coding

A free course for children from Grade 5: make games and art, first with Scratch blocks, then with Python. One 60-minute session a week.

No accounts, no ads, no tracking.
